subject: math.GN
name: Tychonoff's theorem
statement: An arbitrary product of compact topological spaces is compact in the product topology.

subject: math.GN
name: Compact-subset theorem for Hausdorff spaces
statement: Every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.

subject: math.GN
name: Heine–Borel theorem
statement: A subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

subject: math.GN
name: Alexander subbase theorem
statement: If a collection of open sets is a subbase for a topology, the space is compact if and only if every cover by members of that subbase has a finite subcover.

subject: math.GN
name: Urysohn's lemma
statement: In a normal T₁ space, any two disjoint closed sets can be separated by a continuous function to [0,1] that equals zero on one set and one on the other.

subject: math.GN
name: Tietze extension theorem
statement: If A is a closed subset of a normal T₁ space X, every continuous real-valued function on A extends to a continuous real-valued function on X. A function with values in a closed interval can be extended with values in the same interval.

subject: math.GN
name: Urysohn metrization theorem
statement: Every regular T₁ space with a countable basis has a metric inducing its topology.

subject: math.GN
name: Nagata–Smirnov metrization theorem
statement: A topological space is metrizable if and only if it is regular T₁ and has a basis that is a countable union of locally finite families.

subject: math.GN
name: Baire category theorem
statement: In a complete metric space, or in a locally compact Hausdorff space, the intersection of countably many dense open sets is dense.

subject: math.GN
name: Stone–Čech compactification theorem
statement: Every completely regular Hausdorff space X embeds densely in a compact Hausdorff space βX such that every continuous map from X to a compact Hausdorff space extends uniquely to βX.

subject: math.GN
name: One-point compactification theorem
statement: A noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space X has a compact Hausdorff compactification obtained by adjoining one point. Neighborhoods of the new point are complements of compact subsets of X, together with that point.

subject: math.GN
name: Tube lemma
statement: If X is compact and an open subset of X × Y contains X × {y}, then it contains X × V for some open neighborhood V of y in Y.

subject: math.GN
name: Wallace theorem
statement: If A ⊆ X and B ⊆ Y are compact and an open subset U of X × Y contains A × B, there are open neighborhoods V of A and W of B with V × W ⊆ U.

subject: math.GN
name: Cantor intersection theorem
statement: A nested sequence of nonempty closed subsets of a complete metric space, whose diameters tend to zero, has an intersection consisting of exactly one point.

subject: math.GN
name: Lebesgue number lemma
statement: For every open cover of a compact metric space there is δ > 0 such that every subset of diameter less than δ lies in some member of the cover.

subject: math.GN
name: Sequential compactness theorem for metric spaces
statement: A metric space is compact if and only if every sequence in it has a convergent subsequence with limit in the space.

subject: math.GN
name: Invariance of domain
statement: If U is open in Euclidean n-space and f: U → Euclidean n-space is continuous and injective, then f(U) is open and f is a homeomorphism onto its image.

subject: math.GN
name: Brouwer fixed-point theorem
statement: Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space has a fixed point.

subject: math.GN
name: Stone's paracompactness theorem
statement: Every metric space is paracompact: every open cover has an open locally finite refinement.

subject: math.GN
name: Partition of unity theorem
statement: Every open cover of a paracompact Hausdorff space admits a subordinate locally finite partition of unity: continuous nonnegative functions with sum one, each supported in a member of the cover.
